entities.summary: Carl L. Hart is an American psychologist and neuroscientist who is the Mamie Phipps Clark Professor of Psychology at Columbia University. Hart is known for his research on drug abuse and drug addiction, his advocacy for the legalization of recreational drugs, and his recreational drug use. Hart became the second tenured African-American professor of sciences at Columbia University. He is the author of two books for the general public, High Price: A Neuroscientist's Journey of Self-Discovery that Challenges Everything You Know about Drugs and Society (2013) and Drug Use for Grown-Ups: Chasing Liberty in the Land of Fear (2021).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Carl Hart's research on drug abuse and addiction has significantly impacted public health policy, with his advocacy for recreational drug legalization contributing to changes in US laws. His work has also influenced the development of harm reduction strategies.
